body:
### Description

**Nvim version:** NVIM v0.12.4, Linux x86_64
**vhdl_ls version:** 0.88.0
**How the config is enabled:** `vim.lsp.enable('vhdl_ls')` with the upstream
`lsp/vhdl_ls.lua` unmodified and no `after/lsp/` override.

### Description

`lsp/vhdl_ls.lua` lists `.vhdl_ls.toml` in `root_markers`:

```lua
root_markers = {
  'vhdl_ls.toml',
  '.vhdl_ls.toml',
},
workspace_required = true,
```

`.vhdl_ls.toml` is not a project file. vhdl_ls only ever reads it from the
user's home directory:

```rust
// vhdl_lang/src/config.rs
/// Load configuration file from home folder
fn load_home_config(&mut self, messages: &mut dyn MessageHandler) {
    if let Some(home_dir) = dirs::home_dir() {
        let file_name = home_dir.join(".vhdl_ls.toml");
```

The dotted name appears nowhere else in that file. The workspace-level name is
`vhdl_ls.toml`, without the dot. The docstring in `lsp/vhdl_ls.lua` says the
same ("A file named .vhdl_ls.toml in the user home folder"), as does the
[configuration wiki](https://github.com/VHDL-LS/rust_hdl/wiki/VHDL%E2%80%90LS-Configuration).

Because `root_markers` is priority-ordered, the dotted name is only consulted
when no `vhdl_ls.toml` exists anywhere in the ancestry — which is exactly the
situation for a user keeping global defaults in `~/.vhdl_ls.toml`. For those
users, opening any `.vhd` file under `$HOME` outside a configured project
resolves `root_dir` to `$HOME`.

The server confirms it treats that as the workspace root:

```
Library mapping is unknown due to missing vhdl_ls.toml config file in the
workspace root path: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
R=/tmp/vhdlls-repro && rm -rf $R && mkdir -p $R/home/flat $R/home/proj $R/home/vendor
printf 'package vendor_pkg is end package;\n' > $R/home/vendor/vendor_pkg.vhd
cat > $R/home/.vhdl_ls.toml <<'EOF'
standard = "2008"

[libraries]
vendor.files = ['vendor/*.vhd']
vendor.is_third_party = true
EOF
printf 'entity counter is end entity;\n' > $R/home/flat/counter.vhd
cp $R/home/flat/counter.vhd $R/home/proj/counter.vhd
printf "[libraries]\ndefaultlib.files = ['*.vhd']\n" > $R/home/proj/vhdl_ls.toml
cat > $R/probe.lua <<'EOF'
vim.opt.runtimepath:prepend(assert(vim.env.LSPCONFIG_FORK))
vim.lsp.enable('vhdl_ls')
vim.cmd.edit(vim.env.TARGET)
vim.wait(8000, function() return #vim.lsp.get_clients({ bufnr = 0 }) > 0 end, 100)
local c = vim.lsp.get_clients({ bufnr = 0 })[1]
print(c and ('root_dir = ' .. tostring(c.root_dir)) or 'no client attached')
vim.cmd('qa!')
EOF
# LSPCONFIG_FORK = a checkout of this repo
env HOME=$R/home LSPCONFIG_FORK=... TARGET=$R/home/flat/counter.vhd nvim --clean -l $R/probe.lua
```

**Actual:** `root_dir = /tmp/vhdlls-repro/home`
**Expected:** no client attached, consistent with `workspace_required = true`,
since there is no VHDL workspace here.

Running the same probe against `$R/home/proj/counter.vhd` gives
`root_dir = .../home/proj`, and removing `~/.vhdl_ls.toml` entirely gives
`no client attached`. The home-directory file is the only variable that changes
the outcome.

I also tested removing `.vhdl_ls.toml` from `root_markers` locally: the
no-project case becomes `no client attached`, and the case with a project
`vhdl_ls.toml` is unchanged.

### History

This wasn't one decision, so it may be worth laying out:

- #2504 added this config with `single_file_support = true`, so a VHDL file
  outside any project attached with `root_dir = nil`.
- #3659 migrated to `vim.lsp.config` (330 new files). That field has no
  equivalent in the new API, but `workspace_required` defaults to false, so
  behavior was unchanged.
- #4494 set `workspace_required = true`, which removed the single-file attach.
  I authored that one and did not consider this case.

So `$HOME` as a root has been reachable since 2023, but only became the *only*
remaining way these users get a server after #4494.

### Questions

1. Should `.vhdl_ls.toml` be dropped from `root_markers`? Excluding `$HOME` or
   moving to a `root_dir` function would produce the same result, since `$HOME`
   is the only place that file can be, so removal seems like the simplest form
   of the same fix.
2. If so, should `vhdl_ls` gain a `.git` fallback? Every other HDL config here
   has one — `ghdl_ls` (`hdl-prj.json`, `.git`), `verible`
   (`verible.filelist`, `.git`), `svls` (`.git`), `veridian` (`.git`) — and
   none of them sets `workspace_required`. Without a fallback, `vhdl_ls` would
   be the only one that fails to attach in an ordinary git-tracked VHDL project
   with no `vhdl_ls.toml`.

Happy to send a PR for whichever direction you prefer.

comment_data.body:
> `.vhdl_ls.toml` is not a project file. vhdl_ls only ever reads it from the user's home directory:

If it's user config and not a project file, then it shouldn't be in root_markers. 

But it's worth checking the file history and see who originally added it, and @-mention them here (or in your new PR).

@justinmk Checked the history: the marker came in with the config in #2504
(491feed8, March 2023) by @fmaggi, and was carried into `lsp/vhdl_ls.lua`
unchanged by the 0.11 migration in #3659.

@fmaggi — flagging since you added it: dropping it means a VHDL file outside a
project with its own `vhdl_ls.toml` no longer gets an attach, given
`workspace_required = true`.

PR: #4506

title: vhdl_ls: `.vhdl_ls.toml` root marker resolves root_dir to $HOME
